draft.title: Evidence for evolution
card: Fossils are preserved remains or traces of past life. Deeper rock layers are usually older, so fossils in layers show how living things changed over time.
Some animals have similar bone patterns in limbs that do different jobs, such as a human arm, a bat wing and a whale flipper. This points to a shared ancestor.
DNA is the code that carries an organism's instructions. Species with more similar DNA are usually more closely related, and share a more recent ancestor.
Species found on Earth are spread in patterns that match their ancestry. Island species often resemble those on the nearest mainland, which suggests they descended from them.
draft.remember: Fossils, bones, DNA and where species live all point to shared ancestors.

a.q: Scientists find that two species have very similar DNA. What does this most suggest?
opts: They share a fairly recent common ancestor
They live in the same habitat today
They have exactly the same bone structures
One species evolved from the other directly
a.why: More similar DNA usually means a more recent shared ancestor. It does not show that one species came from the other, because both can descend from a common ancestor.
a.clue: Think about how closely related species share ancestors.

b.q: A fossil hunter finds a simple fossil in a deep rock layer and a more complex relative in a higher layer. What does this best show?
opts: Living things in this group changed over time
Both organisms lived at exactly the same time
The higher fossil must have evolved from the lower one
The deeper rock layer formed after the higher one
b.why: Deeper layers are usually older, so the fossils show a change in the group over time. The fossils alone do not prove that the higher one descended directly from the lower one.
b.clue: Which layer is usually older, and what does a change between layers show?

a.best: They share a fairly recent common ancestor

b.best: Living things in this group changed over time
